feedback.issue: Error handling pattern uses dead code that will never execute
feedback.details: All call sites use the pattern: $(sanitize_input "$2") || { echo "..."; exit 1; }. The function always succeeds (never returns non-zero), so the || clause is unreachable. The sanitization still works correctly, but the pattern is misleading.
feedback.suggestion: Option 1 (Preferred): Simplify to TASK_ID=$(sanitize_input "$2") since the function is guaranteed to succeed. Option 2: Add explicit validation like [[ -n "$(sanitize_input \"$2\")" ]] || exit 1 if zero-length output is a concern. Current implementation is functionally correct and safe; this is purely a code clarity suggestion.
feedback.security_impact: None - This is a code style issue, not a security problem. The sanitization still works correctly.
